scenarios.title: Directive: workplace overload walks ABCDE to the close

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

checks.detail: no body check-in in or after the framework

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI grounds the conversation in the person's actual work examples and introduces ABCDE with permission. The biggest problems are repeatedly eliciting information already supplied, using a reflective script instead of concise Directive leadership, and presenting stronger interpretations than the person has reached. Build from the known event and belief, ask only for missing information, and accept the reported improvement without qualifying it.

scenarios.title: Reflective: career comparison walks a framework to the close

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

checks.detail: no body check-in in or after the framework

scenarios.judge_summary: The strongest elements are sustained attention to the career concern, consent before ABCDE, and an actionable manager script. The main priorities are to stop turning uncertainty into asserted conclusions, provide practical wording as soon as the person needs it, and replace repetitive, literary analysis with brief, warm reflections that allow a natural close.

scenarios.title: Supportive: a set declined in words is not offered again

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI meets the central TC-03 requirement: it never reoffers a framework after the refusal and largely stays supportive. The main problems are confident interpretations the person has not reached and repetitive, scripted reflections, especially near the end. Shorter acknowledgments and more room for her mixed feelings would help her feel more accurately understood.

scenarios.title: The three lead-in buttons give three different experiences

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: The strongest element is the initial connection to the manager's slide feedback and the person's stated goal. The main problems are unsupported certainty, repetitive reflection in a directive conversation, and a generic, overlong “Not sure” response. Only that button path is shown; the distinct demonstration and immediate-tool paths remain untested.

scenarios.title: A clear belief in the first message is not a reason to offer early

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: The main failure is withholding the quick, in-chat help the user repeatedly requests while offering a library before understanding the situation. The eventual ABCDE sequence uses relevant details and follows the correct order, but needlessly re-asks known information. MANI also needs to preserve the distinction between wanting to withdraw and actually withdrawing.

scenarios.title: Vague answers: Mani digs deeper without circling or repeating

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: The main problem is overinterpretation: MANI turns tentative descriptions into a much fuller account of isolation than the person supplied, even after they caution against exaggeration. It also repeats the same inquiry about sleep and company instead of consistently deepening, and its poetic reflections weaken the plain, natural acknowledgment the scenario needs. It does maintain one question per turn and avoids imposing a framework.

scenarios.title: A new conversation carries nothing from an earlier one

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: The response appropriately avoids premature advice and asks just one relevant question. It most needs a warmer acknowledgment instead of a restatement, closer attention to Priya's repeated behavior, and removal of the unsupported assumption that the person saw Biscuit every day. No earlier-conversation information appears, but the supplied excerpt cannot establish isolation across two conversations.

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

Earlier responses need less repetitive paraphrasing, cleaner open questions, and greater care not to turn assumptions about the apology or scheduling sequence into facts.

scenarios.title: Give me a tool starts the exercise at once

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI retains the central details and uses plain language, but it delays practical help and does not meet the scenario's requirement to begin the tool without preamble. It should build on the event already provided, ask one useful question at a time, and replace repetitive paraphrases and assumed timing with concise, directive help.

scenarios.title: An upcoming holiday, a past one and two people kept apart

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI keeps the coming Thursday central and offers useful, modest planning suggestions without imposing a framework. The main fixes are to preserve the friend's trip timing and avoid inferred circumstances, replace near-verbatim reflections with brief natural acknowledgments, and follow the Directive style with fewer exploratory questions and clearer next steps.

scenarios.title: A real workplace problem is not disputed as a thought

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI recognizes the doubled workload and elicits the person's desired outcome, but then redirects a real workplace problem into repetitive cognitive-framework work. It should distinguish the anticipated reaction from the actual workload, avoid unsupported assumptions, and provide concise practical help seeking acknowledgment, reprioritization, or coverage.

scenarios.title: A practical workload problem gets options first

checks.source: Lolly's test emails, 2026-11-23 (assumptions stated as facts); approved by muhammad 2026-11-24

scenarios.judge_summary: MANI does well at offering concrete workload options immediately after the practical request, without disputing the user's assessment or introducing a therapeutic framework. The main failures are unsupported assumptions about acceptable delivery and managerial responses, an incomplete revision that misses the requested wording, and continued instruction after the user has a satisfactory plan.
